newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to deliver delayed arms shipment to Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to deliver delayed arms shipment to Bosnia.

text.p: The United States will begin delivering a shipload of military hardware to Bosnia following the ousting of two defense officials in the country's Muslim-Croat federation, the State Department said Wednesday.

Spokesman Glyn Davies said the ship American Condor, which has been standing off the coast of Croatia, "will proceed to the port of Ploce and begin offloading the U.S. military equipment for further delivery to the Bosnian Federation".

Davies told reporters the delivery would go ahead now that Federation President Kresimir Zubak had accepted the resignation of Defense Minister Vladimir Soljic and agreed to replace Deputy Defense Minister Hasan Cengic as of Wednesday.

"We now have in hand copies of the written orders making these changes from Zubak's office, and we have also received assurances from Bosnian President (Alija) Izetbegovic that Mr Cengic is no longer serving as deputy minister," he said.

Washington alleged that Cengic, a Muslim, had close ties with Iran and was likely to obstruct the U.S.-sponsored "Train and Equip" program for the Federation's armed forces, of which the arms delivery is a key component.

Its objections to Soljic, a Croat, were less clear. He resigned Tuesday after rumors began circulating he would be forced to step down along with Cengic as part of a package deal which would be billed as a reorganisation.
